8265.c: A handwritten Persian language manuscript in the nastaliq script of the 'Kulliyat-i Sa'di', composed of six Risālas (treatises) by the poet Sheikh Sa'dī Shirazi, including Gulistān, Bustān, Persian qasāʾid, marathi, Muthalathāt, Tarjiʿāt, badāʾiʿ, arranged by ʿAlī bin Aḥmad Bīsutum in 726 AH (1326) with this copy probably completed by ʿAlī bin Aḥmad bin Abī Naṣr. The text is in black with some headings in red, within ruled borders of blue and gold and compartments of gold lines, written on glazed paper. The title is illuminated. The volume is bound in stamped Persian binding. The work includes commentary on the origin of the volume and the creator has copied the mulakhkhaṣ of Ṭayyibāt of Saʿdī and arranged them in alphabetical order.

11181.c: A handwritten and illustrated Persian language manuscript in the nastaliq script of Yūsuf va Zulaykhā (Yusuf and Zulaikha), by Jami, originally composed in the 15th century as part of Jami's Haft Awrang (Seven Thrones), with this copy completed on 20 Rabīʿ al-Awwal 1245 (19 September 1829). The text is in black with section headings in red, within ruled borders of gold and black, written on paper. The title is illuminated. The volume contains three miniatures on leaf 6a, leaf 22a, and leaf 29b. The first miniature presents the ascension night (miʿrāj) of Muhammad with a winged-horse, called Burāq. The second shows the image of Zulaykhā and her servants.

12199.d: Copied in the late 16th or early 17th century
a: Kashifi, Husayn Wa'iz حسين واعظ كاشفى
12199.c: Mawahib‐e 'Aliyyah, or Tafsir‐e Husayni, is a Persian commentary (tafsīr) on chapters of the Qurʾān along with the Persian translation of verses by Husayn Wa'iz Kashifi. The verses are written in red and the commentary and translation in black. It seems that it is the commentary of the last juzʾ (part thirty) of the Qurʾān which starts with Q 78 and ends with Q 114. It has been wrongly described on the wrapper as the ‘Koran’ (see image 405).

a: Abū ʿAbdallāh Muḥammad b. Saʿīd al-Azdī al-Qalḥātī ابي عبدالله محمد بن سعيدالازدي القلهاتي
12748.c: This work is divided into two parts (a) fifty (50) chapters regarding tawhīd al-manān and dhikr āyāt al-Qurʾān; and (b) the creation of the heavens and earth, the prophets (anbiyāʾ), religions, opinions held by Arabs during jāhiliyya (so-called ignorant era); religions of India, on ʿabdat andʿibādat al-shams, ʿabdat and ʿibādat al-qamar (worshippers and the worshipping of Sun and Moon); Jewish sects; Christian sects; on infidels; on Muʿtazilah and Qadariyyah; Abāziyyah; Khawārij; Shīʿisim which includes 27 sects: (Kaysāniyyah; Mukhtāriyyah; Hāshimiyyah; Banāniyyah (Bayāniyyah); al-Zarāmiyah; al-Zaydiyyah; al-Jārūdiyyah; al-Sulaymāniyyah; al-Ṣālihiyyah; al-Imāmiyyah; al-Bāqiriyyah wa ’l-Jaʿfariyyah; al-Nāwnusiyyah? (al-Nāwusiyyah); Ismāʿiliyyah; al-Abṭaḥiyyah; al-Shamaṭiyyah (al-Simṭiyyah); etc. The first part was completed on Monday morning, the first day of Ramadan 1124 AH by Saʿīd ʿAfīf Khalf Sulaymān ʿAbdallāh al-Ḥajdarī. Copyist (nāsikh) is ʿAbdallāh Mubārak whose poetic/literary notes are seen in this book. An embossed note on the spine reads: ‘Inna-mā al-Aʿmāl bi ’l-niyyāt’, which is a prophetic tradition that means: ‘(The value of) an action depends on the intention behind it.’ Authoritative theological text written for Sunni Muslims. Contains 50 chapters. Arguments, the Koran, expplanations, rules, justice. Ch. 49 On the copier of the manuscript. Written/copied by Abu Abdullah Mohammed Bin Saed Al-Azadi Al-Omani Al-Abadhi Al-Qulhati. Former owner: Mohammed Nasser Khal

14194.c: Collection contains an undecorated parchment scroll of the Megillat Esther (אסתר מגילת) in Ashkenazi square script (Northern Europe), dated late 18th century, with visible stitching of membranes. The scroll is wound onto a single wooden rod affixed to its left extremity and features a protective textile edge/wrapper. The latter is typical of Esther scrolls created in Holland or by someone with knowledge of Dutch traditions.

17404.c: A Czech translation of 'Historia destructionis Troiae' by Guido de Colomna (also known as Guido de Columnis or Guido delle Colonne). Guido omitted to give this work an official title so it is known by multiple titles, with 'Historia Destructionis Troiae' being sourced from the 'destructionis' of the Prologue's heading. Binding: Early 19th century boards with corners and spine in white-painted vellum. Paper spine label: 'Bohemian siege of Troy'. Collation: Lacking at least a gathering at beginning, and single leaves after ff. 169, 181 and 191, and an unknown number of leaves at end, else apparently complete. Layout: Written in 26-29 long lines, ruled in brown ink. Script: Gothic cursive book-hand. Decoration: 31 of 4-9 line, mostly 6-8 line, decorated initials. Painted in two colours on contrasting rectangular grounds, in the same range of colours often tonally shaded to give a sense of receding geometric shapes. Acanthus borders. 2-line red initials throughout. Many marginal additions and annotations, mostly post-medieval. Catalogued from item in hand, catalogue cards and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Other Title(s): Historia destructionis Troiae. Czech. Kroniky Trojanske [title previously supplied by cataloguer]; Bohemian siege of Troy; History of the siege of Troy; History of the destruction of Troy; Kroniky Trojanske; The Trojan Chronicles

17669.t: Le livre de Boèce de consolacion
17669.c: Prologue of Jean de Meun addressed to Philip IV of France (1285-1314), followed by a French translation by an anonymous translator. Binding: Post-medieval (probably 17th century) vellum over pasteboards. Lettered on spine: 'Boece de la consolat'. Layout: Written in 33 lines ruled in plummet with glosses on each side or interrupting the text and written the full width of the page within bounding-lines 148 mm wide. Script: Written in lettre batarde. Decoration: Miniature (f.7; 8.6 x 8.4 cm), showing the translator dictating his work to a scribe, heads the prologue. 6 decorated initials (3- to 6- line) introduce the prologue and each of the five books. 1- and 2- line initials with penwork infilling. Other Title(s): De consolatione philosophiae. French. Le livre de Boèce de consolacion [title previously supplied by cataloguer]; Boece de la consolat

17925.c: A collection of poems by the Italian humanist, poet, and writer Petrarch with the vast majority written in sonnet form. Binding: post-medieval (probably 17th century) vellum. Paper endpapers. Marginalia signed by Sir George Grey on endpapers. Collation: i-xi8, xii6, xiii10, xiv-xv8, with catchwords. Text ends 36 poems short of the full set and presumably leaves are missing at the end, though the text may have been copied from a short exemplar. Layout: Single column, 27-29 lines, ruled in faint plummet; written space 16.2 x 9.5 cm with versal initials in a vertical column ruled 7 mm wide to the left of the text. Script: Rounded Italian humanistic minuscule. Decoration: There are 319 of 2-line historiated initials in burnished gold on blue, green and red grounds outlined in black with white tracery, introducing individual sonnets and canzoni. On f.1, 8-line historiated initial 'V' in a gold frame begins the first sonnet - showing Petrarch writing at his desk while cupid aims an arrow at his heart. The opening folio has a full border of white-vine design framed by ruled gold lines. Erased coat of arms in lower border. For fuller description of the border images, see Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). In the style of Ambrogio da Marliano. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Other title(s): Canzoniere. Italian. Canzoniere [title previously supplied by cataloguer]; Il Canzoniere; Rime Sparse; Rerum vulgarium fragmenta; Fragmen

18270.c: A lectionary which gives Gospel readings for use on Sundays. Binding: Bound in medieval wooden boards. Upper board with decorated textile covering, lower board bare, rebacked, lacking clasps. Modern leather loose cover. Lettered on spine: 'Novum Testamentum Graece'. Collation: i-xii8, xiii6 [of 8, lacking ii-iii], xiv-xx8, xxi7, with signatures in Greek letters; lacking 2 leaves after page 194, last 7 leaves are later additions. Layout: Single column, 24 lines, ruled in blind; written space 18.3 x 11.7 cm. Script: Written in a regular Greek minuscule bookhand. Decoration: A large 3-sided headpiece, in red and black, introduces the Gospels on page 1 - motifs include geometric shapes, curling leaves and corner palmettes. Another 4 interlaced ropework headpieces in ink, infilled with red and yellow, mark textual divisions at pages 75, 111, 233 and 253. 163 2-line initials (to page 254, end of gathering 16 only) drawn in designs in ink, infilled with red and yellow. Decoration: Headings in red uncials, neumes throughout in red; some initials in red and some heightened further in yellow. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description. Other Title(s): Bible. N.T. Epistles and Gospels, Liturgical. Greek Gospel lectionary [title previously supplied by cataloguer]; Novum Testamentum Graece; Lectionarum graecum

18685.c: The four Gospels in Greek, preceded by the Canon Tables, comprising St Matthew (ff.5-63), St Mark (ff.64-98v), St Luke (ff.101-159v) and St John (ff.160-199). Added at the end are the lections for the week after Easter, breaking off imperfectly. Binding: Nineteenth century brown morocco over wooden boards. Lettered on spine: 'Evangelia IV Graece. Ms. in membranis M.CXXVIII'. Collation: i4, ii-viii8, ix7 [of 8, lacking iv], x-xiii8, xiv7 [of 8, lacking ii], xv-xx8, xxi7 [of 8, lacking vi], xxii-xxv8, xxvi6 [of 8, lacking vii-viii], with signatures in Greek in upper outer corners of the first page of each gathering; lacking single leaves after ff.63, 100 and 159, and lacking at least 2 leaves at end. Layout: Single column, mostly 26-lines, ruled in blind, written space 14 x 9 cm. Script: Written in a calligraphic Greek minuscule. Text in black with headings, foot notes, some side-notes and versal initials in red throughout. Decoration: Four full-page Canon Tables on ff.1-2v are framed by arched columns drawn in black and infilled with interlace in red and yellow wash. The arches are surmounted by crosses and palmettes. Five decorative headpieces introduce the Gospels and the list of liturgical readings at the end. They are drawn in red with cross, foliate and arabesque designs. Titles and opening initials are painted in matching red. The headpieces are rectangular (5.6 x 9 cm, f.5), oblong (ff.64, 160 and 199v) or three-sided (f.101). Ropework headpieces introduce lists of chap

18944.c: Three of the greatest scientific textbooks, written by Aristotle, which were of central importance in academic life during the Middle Ages. These books are the Latin translation by William of Moerbeke (c1215-1286). Binding: Rebound in 2007. Text block resewn and limp vellum binding replaced 19th century paper covers (roughly stitched), fastened to the manuscript with leather straps. Collation: i-vi8, vii10, viii-xi8, xii7 [of 8, final blank cancelled], xii-xiv12; with catchwords and signatures. Layout: Double column, 36-37 lines, ruled in plummet. Written space 20.6 x 15 cm. Script: Written in a large, slightly sloping angular gothic text hand with dark brown ink. Latin, with a few glosses in a contemporary small well-formed script and many side-notes in a rough 14th century hand in a cursive script, and a few later notes. Decoration: 2-line initials in red or blue, with contrasting penwork. 26 initials (one each 7- and 5- line, fifteen 4-line, nine 3-line) in divided red and blue, with penwork in both colours and full-length marginal extensions, marking the introduction of each book. The colophons on ff.58 and 121 are crossed through in red and the rubrication on f.121 adds a spotted dog, with a bell around its neck, urinating into a pot. It grasps the last flourish of the Explicit in its mouth. Paragraph marks throughout in red and blue, running-titles alternately in red and blue letters. Leaf f.109v has a diagram (8 x 8 cm) which forms part of text, and leaf f.115v has a g

19347.c: The Divinae Institutiones of Lucius Caelius Firmianus Lactantius, the Christian Cicero of the third century, was highly regarded in the Renaissance for the elegance of its literary style and became the first book printed in Italy (1465). Binding: Post-medieval (probably sixteenth or early seventeenth century) Italian limp vellum. Binding includes a flange cut from an early printed book: Quaestiones in Universalia Porphyrii, Quaestiones in Aristotelis Praedicamenta, Quaestiones in Aristotelis libros De interpretatione (lib. I). Antonius Andreae: Quaestiones in Gilberti Porretani Librum sex principiorum. Venice: Reynaldus de Novimagio and Theodorus de Reynsburch (Hain *6441, ISTC No. id00387000), not after 1479. Collation: i-xix10, xx8 (of 10, blank ix-x cancelled), mostly with catchwords. Text complete. Layout: Single column, 33 lines, ruled in plummet. Written space 19.2 x 11.5 cm. Script: Early round humanistic miniscule with some gothic features. Hand resembles that of Coluccio Salutati (1331-1406), although it seems likely that more than one scribe worked on this manuscript. Some guidewords for the rubricator remain. Some textual corrections and side-notes in contemporary hands. Decoration: Five large initials (3 of 8-line, 2 of 7-line) in mauve or red. 3-line initials throughout in red or blue with vertical flourished penwork in mauve or red. Empty spaces also exist, e.g. on f.1 and f.171v, where more elaborate decorative initials were likely planned to be added. Catalogu

19992.c: Third part of St Gregory's commentary on the book of Job. Binding: 19th century English calf with 4 raised bands. Preserves the sides of a 16th century English blind-stamped binding with panels of the royal arms and Tudor rose flanked by angels and lozenge-shaped stamps of a pelican in her piety and of a rosette. Number XXIX in gilt on a dark red morocco label at the foot of the spine. Binder's spine title: 'Gregori magni comment in Jobum vel moralia'. Collation: i-xvi8, xvii13 [of 14, blank i cancelled], xviii-xxxviii8, xxxix6 [of8, blank vii-viii cancelled], with some catchwords. Layout: ff.1-128, double column, 42 lines, ruled in plummet, written space 27.2 x 17.9 cm. ff.129-141, double column, 40 lines ruled in plummet, written space 26.7 x 18.5 cm. ff.142-315v, double column, 40 lines, ruled in plummet, written space 26.5 x 18.2 cm. Script: Written by 4 scribes: Scribes 1 and 2 use an early gothic bookhand. Scribe 3 uses a larger well-formed hand. Scribe 1, ff.1-52v; Scribe 2, ff.52v-128; Scribe 3, ff.129-141; and Scribe 4, ff.142-315v. Decoration: Part 1, Scribe 1 (f.1) features a crudely painted initial in green with blue foliate design on red infill and dull pink surround patterned with tracery and geometric designs. Part 1, Scribe 1 and Scribe 2, (ff. 11v, 21v, 28, 41, 53, 66v, 77v, 91v, 101, 113, 119) has initials in green and-or red ink with brown and yellow penwork. Part 2, Scribe 3 (f.129) has initial in blue ink with red penwork. Part 3, Scribe 4 (f.142) has pai

20078.c: A collection of short biographies of 106 famous historical and mythological women, from Eve to Joan, Queen of Naples. Composed by Florentine author Giovanni Boccaccio in Latin about 1361. Binding: 19th century blue paper over boards. Collation: i-ii12, iii14 [last 2 originally blank]. Table of contents (ff.36-36v). Text complete. Layout: Single column, 55-62 lines, ruled in ink (outer bounding lines only). Written space 25 x 15 cm. Script: Small German cursive bookhand. Many early added side-notes additions on last 2 leaves. Decoration: One 8-line calligraphic initial on f.1v. One 12-line decorated initial introduces text on f.1. Extends to form a border along the left and lower margins. Headings and about 100 of 3-line initials in red. Capitals touched in red. Other Title(s): De mulieribus claris; De praeclaris mulieribus; Concerning Famous Women

20879.c: A liturgical manuscript produced in Perugia probably in the late 1470s and originally owned by Father Antonius de Macerata. A breviary is a service book containing the texts necessary for the performance of the church’s official religious services with a liturgical calendar, and this example is laid out in the traditional form. Title supplied by cataloguer. Contents: f.1 - Invitatories; ff.1v-60v - Ferial psalter; ff.61-240v - Temporal; ff.241-345v - Sanctoral; ff.345-384v - Communal; ff.386-391v - Calendar. Binding: Bound in early 19th century English calf, rebacked with spine laid on; gilt stamped decorations on spine; gilt rules on both boards; and green endpapers. On added paper endpaper: 'Brevianum Romanum Sec. XV. Spine title: Lectionarum cum calendrio M.S. Memb: sec:xv. cum depictis initialibus'. Endleaves from a 14th century Italian manuscript of the Decretals of Boniface VIII. Collation: i-xxxix10 with catchwords. Text complete. Layout: Double column, 33 lines, ruled in pale ink, written space 19.8 x 15 cm. Script: Rounded gothic liturgical hand in two size; rubrics in red. Decoration: Folios 1v, 306v and 307 have full borders filled with fine brown tendril sprays of leaves, buds, fruits and flowers, inhabited by butterflies and winged putti in colours of blue, plum-red, green, pink, brown and gold. On f.1v the Beatus initial is integrated with the border decoration with luxuriant leafy extensions and a large long-necked bird set on its patterned gold surround relate

21131.c: Two of Cicero's great philosophical texts. 'De Divinatione' is about ancient Roman divination and was written in 44 BC. There are about 30 pages missing at the end of this copy. 'De Natura Deorum' discusses theological views about Hellenistic philosophies and was written in 45 BC. Only a few words are missing from the end of this copy. Binding: Contemporary Florentine goatskin over thin wooden boards blindstamped with outer border of repeated impressions of a rectangular arabesque tool and inner compartment formed on a circle within a rectangle made up of repeated impressions of small ropework tools and small plugs. Spine intact. Fragments of 4 linen clasps on upper cover secured by foliate metal pins. Collation: i-iii10, iv-xi10, xii7 [of 8, final leaf mostly torn away], with catchwords lacking probably 3 gatherings (40 leaves) after quire 3 (f.30); otherwise complete. Layout: Single column, 26 lines, ruled in pale ink. Written space 13.9 x 8.9 cm. Script: Round, rather clubbed, Italian humanist bookhand. Decoration: Headings in pale red capitals with opening lines of each main section in pale red capitals (except f.31 where they are in black capitals touched with red). Four initials in burnished gold (5- or 6- lines) decorated with white-vine introduce the books on ff.1, 31, 56v and 95v. Faded red and green infills, set on blue grounds. Patterning of the grounds by clusters of white dots. From the initials, on ff.56v and 95v, an ivy-leaf spray extends along the vertical bor

21642.c: This Roman Missal, which contains the text used for the celebration of Mass together with a liturgical calendar, is bound in two volumes where volume 1 is catalogued as MedMS-G138 (this record) and volume 2 is catalogued as MedMS-139. Some details are replicated in the records of both volumes. For additional detail and commentary on both volumes, see Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Contents (volume 1): ffii-viii5 - Calendar; ff.1-147 - Temporal from Advent to Holy Sunday; ff.147v-152v - Preface chants for solemn feasts and ferial days; f.153 - Prayers before Mass; ff.153v-157v - Ordinary of the Mass, including chants for commencement of Gloria and Preface; ff. 159-166v - Canon of the Mass, including chants for Te igitur; ff.167-199v - Sanctoral from Advent to Easter; ff.199v-233 - Common of the Saints and Votive Masses, including Mass for the Dead; ff.233-235v - Prayers before and thanksgiving after Mass. Binding: Bound in dark blue morocco with gilt tooling. Edges gauffred and gilt. Lettered on the spine: 'Missale'. Collation (volume 2): i6, ii-iii8, iv7 [vi cancelled], v-xvi8, xvii6, xviii-xli8, xlii4 [sixteenth century]. Catchword, written vertically, at end of each gathering. Layout: Double column, 32 lines, ruled in pale red ink. Written space 20 x 13.5 cm. Script: Written in a very fine gothic liturgical hand in three different sizes for liturgical directions, ordinary text and Canon respectively. The last 6 pages of volume 1 and the last gathering of volume 2 are in

22307.c: This Roman Missal, which contains the text used for the celebration of Mass together with a liturgical calendar, is bound in two volumes where volume 1 is catalogued as MedMS-G138 and volume 2 is catalogued as MedMS-139 (this record). Some details are replicated in the records of both volumes. For additional detail and commentary on both volumes, see Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Contents (volume 2): ff.1-vi - Calendar; ff.1-110v - Temporal from Easter to the Sunday before Advent (the Exultet is included in the Mass for Pentecost); ff.110v-118v - Preface Chants for special feasts and ferial days; ff.119-123v - Ordinary for the Mass including chants for opening of the Gloria and Preface; ff.125-130v - Canon of the Mass including chants for Te igitur; ff.130v-132v - Prayers after Mass; ff.133-268v - Sanctoral from Easter to Advent; ff.269-315 - Common of the Saints and Votive Masses, including Nuptial Mass and Mass for the Dead; ff.316-319 - Prayers before and thanksgiving after Mass. Collation (volume 2): i6, ii-iii8, iv7 [vi cancelled], v-xvi8, xvii6, xviii-xli8, xlii4 [sixteenth century]. Catchword, written vertically, at end of each gathering. Layout: Double column, 32 lines, ruled in pale red ink. Written space 20 x 13.5 cm. Script: Written in a very fine gothic liturgical hand in three different sizes for liturgical directions, ordinary text and Canon res

22564.c: A florilegium, or anthology of quotations, from the works of St Augustine. List of works from which the quotations are taken at the end of the text: 'Retractationes, De trinitate, Enchiridion ad Laurentium, De Genesi ad litteram, De fide et symbolo, De libero arbitrio'. Binding: Late 19th century leather binding with red leather spine title label and marbled endpapers. Spine title: 'Flores Beati Augustini (MSS)'. Collation: i-ii8, iii-xi10, xii11 [of 12, final blank cancelled]. Text complete. Layout: Written in 39-40 long lines to f74v and thereafter in double columns; ruled in blind. Written space 22 x 15.5 cm. Script: Written in a sloping humanistic cursive script. Decoration: On f.1 is a burnished gold 6-line initial on a blue ground, decorated with white vine. This supports a white-vine border on 3 sides of the page, framed by gold lines. Unframed right-hand margin has 4 gold circlets with radiating hair-line sprays. The repainted cartouche in the centre of the lower border on f.1, now shows a spray of crimson and white flowers in a green field. 3-5 line initials throughout volume in red or blue. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Other title(s): Works. Selections. Latin Flores Sancti Augustini [title previously supplied by cataloguer]; Flores Beati Augustini (MSS)

22787.c: A Christian devotional book, commonly known as the Rossdhu Book of Hours, this volume is richly illuminated with the contents typical of its kind. It was probably produced in Bruges between 1450 and 1475, and its first owner was likely to have been the Countess of Moray, Elizabeth Dunbar, who lived with her third husband at Rossdhu, Scotland. Contents: Pages 1-12 - Calendar; pages 13-23 - the fifteen O's; pages 24-44 - Suffrages in honour of the Trinity and the saints; pages 45-101 - Hours of the Virgin [Use of Sarum]; pages 102-121 - Hymns and prayers in honour of the Virgin; pages 122-131 - Devotions in honour of the Passion; pages 132-133 - Eucharistic devotions; pages 135-145 - Penitential psalms; pages 146-149 - Psalms of degree; pages 149-158 - Litany; pages 159-190 - Office of the Dead [Use of Sarum] ; pages 191-208 - Commendation of Souls; pages 209-217 - Psalms of the Passion; page 218 - Rubric for the psalms of St Jerome. Binding: 19th century dark brown morocco binding, blind-stamped and with gilt edges, later rebound. Lettered on spine: 'Horae B.M.V. ad usum Sarum M.S. xv. cent'. Collation: i6, ii-iv8, v7 [of 8, lacking v], vi-viii8, ix6, x-xiii8, xiv6, xv4. Leaves are paginated 1-218 (i.e. 109 leaves), not foliated, in old ink. Lacking leaf after page 68 (f.34) and further texts at end, otherwise complete. Layout: Single column; 22 lines; frame-ruled. Written space 14.1 x 9.5 cm. Script: Written in Gothic liturgical script. Some early additions to calendar. Decor

23172.c: Latin adaptation by Rufinus of Aquileia (died 410) of the Greek history of the Roman defeat of Palestine, written in 77-78 AD by Flavius Josephus (about 37-100 AD). It is one of 18 manuscripts identified as having been written by the Florentine scribe Domenico di Cassio, of Narni, between about 1445 and 1460 with the decoration being in the style of Filippo di Matteo Torelli. Both were associated with the Florentine bookseller Vespasiano da Bisticci. Binding: Post-medieval (probably 17th century) limp vellum with gilt edges that may be original. Paper endpapers. Collation: i9 [of 10, lacking blank at the beginning], ii-xviii10, xix6; with catchwords or traces of them, and with later leaf signatures. Layout: Single column, 34 lines, ruled in blind. Written space 24.2 x 13.3 cm. Script: Round humanist book hand. Contemporary marginal notes. Decoration: 8 initials (1 of 8-line, 4 of 7-line, 2 of 6-line) in burnished gold introduce the preface and each of the books of the history on ff.1, 3, 43v, 79, 100, 113, 126 and 150. All initials are decorated with white-vine stems, painted on blue, green and red grounds patterned with yellow dots and lightly shaded with a fawn wash. The initial on f.1 has a divided spine, patterned in red crosses in a style reminiscent of 12th century work. f.1 also has a three-quarters border in which white vine stems twist around a notional central axis and in the lower margin they radiate from either side of a centrally placed green wreath held by two w

23175.t: Leaf from a late 15th century Latin Gradual
23175.c: A single manuscript leaf from a Latin Gradual which is a liturgical book that contains the chants for the proper of the mass - those parts that are spoken or sung by the choir or the people: introits, graduals, tracts, alleluia, offertory, communion verses and sequences for special feasts. It may also include chants for the ordinary of the mass - that part that is reasonably constant or selected without regard to date: kyrie, gloria, sanctus, agnus dei; and for the introductory 'asperges' rite. Contents: Gradual chants from the Common of Virgins, most likely Psalms 44:5, and part of Psalms 44:12, although the wording is slightly different from the Vulgate Bible (see transcription). Catalogued from item in hand and information received from donor and Alexandra Barratt. Title supplied by cataloguer.

23730.c: A manuscript that contains chants for the canonical hours of the Divine Office and intended for use in the liturgical choir, this is the second volume of a 2-volume set. The location of volume 1 is unknown. Contents: Comprises the Temporal from the first Sunday in August (f.1, 'Omnis sapientia...') to the Sunday before Advent, the Office for the dedication of a church (f. 56) and the Sanctoral from SS. Peter and Paul (f.75., 29 June) to St Katherine (25 November) with detailed offices for SS. Martin and Cecilia. Music: Contains musical notation. Binding: Post-medieval calf over wooden boards (re-covered but possibly using original boards and fittings) with metal bosses and clasps. 8 bookmark cords. Pastedowns at each end are vellum leaves of earlier manuscripts. Binding - First pastedown (front): 'Life of St Donatus', in Latin, 35.7 x 25 cm, 2 columns, part of 28 lines, ruled in blind, written space 28 x 22.2 cm written in brown ink in a fine rounded Romanesque hand, Italy, early 12th century. Binding - Second pastedown (back): 'Missal', a bifolium, each leaf 24.7 x 19.8 cm, 30 lines, ruled in blind, written space 22.2 x.12.7 cm, written in brown ink in two sizes of a rounded liturgical hand, rubrics in red, versal initials throughout in red, punctus flexus punctuation added in red, Italy, 12-13th century. Binding - Third pastedown (back): Part leaf from a very large unfinished choir book, Italy, 16th century. Collation: i10, ii-vi8, vii5 [of 6, blank vi cancelled], viii10, i

24317.t: Cronica Matthiae Parisiensis aut quæ Historia minor vulgo dicitur Historia
24317.c: An abbreviated version of his history of England by Matthew of Paris, mainly covering 1067 to 1253 or, according to the prologue, after the conquest of England by the leader of the Normans, William (aka Duke of Normandy, William the Conqueror. Preceded by a brief biography of the author. Contents: Leaves 1-9 - blank; Leaves 10-11 - notes about Matthew of Paris and his history signed: 'Roger Twysden, 19 die februarij 1648_9 apud East Peckham'; Leaf 12 - blank; Leaf 13a - title page with note: 'Roger Twysden hunc librum transcribi curavi Ano Dni 1648 pretium 6l. R. T.'; Leaf 13b - blank; Leaf 14a - note certifying that the translation is correct, signed by Sir Roger Twysden and Hamnet Ward, together with note about the connection of the book with the Monastery of St Albans; Leaf 14b - blank; Leaves 15-19 - Prologue, beginning 'Incipit prologus in historiam anglorum post-conquifirionem Anglia a Normannorum duce Willilmo…'; Leaf 20 - blank; Leaves 21-286 - Text; Leaf 287 - notes in the hand of Roger Twysden and Hamnet Ward; Leaves 288-289 - blank; Leaves 290-300 - index; Leaves 301-302 - blank. Binding: Pigskin over boards with raised bands. Vellum flyleaves. Collation: i12, ii14, iii-xxviii10, xxix12, xxx4. Catchword on each page. Index ff.290-300. Leaves 1-9 blank. Paginated from leaf 15-287 as 1-543, omitting leaf 20 (blank). Layout: Written in a single column, 53 lines. Written space 28 x 12.5 cm. Script: Cursive. Decoration: Drawings, including shields in the margin, and man

25041.c: A manuscript Bible, in Latin, comprising the whole of the Old and New Testaments and the Apocrypha, together with introductions to the testaments and prologues, ascribed to St Jerome, to some books. Binding: Modern (circa 1900) limp vellum with ties; gilt edges. Collation: i-xiv10, xv-xxiii12, xxiv11+6 [of 12, ix cancelled and replaced by an extra gathering of 6 leaves, i.e.ff.256-261], xxv-xxvii12, xxviii-xxxix10, xxx6, xxxii11[of 12, lacking ii], xxxiii5 [of 6, final blank cancelled]. Layout: Double column, 53-56 lines, ruled in plummet. Script: Written in a small gothic text hand by more than one scribe. Decoration: headings left blank; running titles alternately in red and blue letters (now cropped in latter part of manuscript). Large initials at the start of every book of the bible divided red and blue with penwork in both colours. 2-line chapter initials in red and blue with contrasting penwork. 1-line versal initials in the Psalms alternately red and blue with simple contrasting penwork. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Other title(s): Bible. Latin. 13th century. Bible [title previously supplied by cataloguer]

25220.c: Chronicle of the popes and the emperors by Martin of Troppau. Two parallel texts with the history of the emperors on every verso and the history of the popes on every recto, ending in 1270 and 1281 respectively. Binding: Bound in post-medieval (probably 17th century) white vellum over pasteboard. Lettered on spine: 'Martin Poloni Cronic. M.S.' Numbered at foot, '16077'. Collation: i-viii10, with catchwords in decorative cartouches and leaf signatures. Text complete. Layout: Single column, 33-37 lines, bounding lines ruled in plummet. Written space 16.5 x 9.7 cm. Script: Written in dark brown ink in a rounded gothic bookhand. Decoration: f.3 - A large painted 10-line initial introduces the Preface. It consists of acanthus leaf design in red, green, blue and lilac heightened with white tracery, on a burnished gold ground, with a 3-sided matching leaf border entwined around intersecting brown bars and embellished with gold bezants. 3-line initials throughout in red and blue with vertical flourished penwork in brown or red. Headings, dates and running-titles in red. Capitals touched in red on f.1v only. Paragraph marks throughout in red and blue. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989)

25587.c: A selection of texts arranged for the use of Dominican nuns. Contents: Text opens 'De sancta Barbara virgine & martire, Oratio…' with 9 readings, followed by readings for the Conception of the Virgin, St Anthony, the translation of Thomas Aquinas, SS. Ignatius, Kunegund, Thomas Aquinas, Albert, the translation of St Peter Martyr, the Apparition of St Michael, etc. and including SS. Henry, Sebald, Wenceslas, and the Lance and Nails. Binding: Modern (c.1900) plain brown pigskin by the Guild of Women-Binders (London, England); gilt edges; green marbled endpapers. Spine title: 'MS'. Collation: i-xxxi8, xxii6+1, with catchwords. Layout: Single column, 20 lines, ruled in black ink. Written space 13.6 x 8.9 cm. Script: Gothic liturgical hand. Decoration: 2-line blue initial on f.1 with red penwork infilling and full-length penwork flourishes in red. Decoration: A few 1-line capitals in red or blue. 2-line initials throughout in red or blue. Rubrics in red. Capitals touched in red. Some of the rubrics are in German. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Title supplied by cataloguer

25800.c: History of all the nations that had been conquered by the Romans, written in Greek in the second century by Appian. The text was translated into Latin by Pietro Candido Decembri (1399-1477) and was dedicated to Nicholas V (Pope from 1447-1455). Contents: Prologue is followed by the text itself on f2v. There was evidently a leaf missing from the exemplar: f.41v breaks off 6 lines from the top and the rest of that page, f.42 and the first 7 lines of f.43 are left blank. f.41v. is marked by another scribe: 'Defectus unius folii in quo tumultus populi contineri videbatur…'. Binding: 18th century (probably Italian) mottled calf. Spine gilt, with author and title 'Appian_Alex_Histor' in gilt on pale orange label at top of spine and 'MS_In Mem.' in gilt on black label at bottom of spine. Gilt edges. Marbled endpapers on verso of boards only. Catalogue entry pasted on. Collation: i-x10, with vertical catchwords within cruciform flourishes and with signatures. Text complete. Layout: Single column, 20 lines, ruled in blind. Written space 14.7 x 10 cm. Script: Written in a well-spaced round humanistic script. Side-notes by scribe in pale red. Headings towards the beginning by another scribe in bright red. Decoration: Four burnished initials (5- to 6- line) introduce the preface, prologue and Books I and III on ff.1, 2v, 11, and 53v. Space was also left for an initial to introduce Book II. The initials are decorated with white-vine on purplish red and green grounds with yellow dots outli

26251.c: A liturgical manuscript produced in Naples for use by the Benedictine’s, this breviary contains the texts necessary for their performance of the church’s official religious services. Contents: ff.1-6v - Calendar including St Benedict as duplex maius (21 March) and St Januarius of Naples (19 September) in red; f.7-12v Rubrics - interpretation of calendar and degree of feasts; ff.13-94v - Temporal (diurnal) from first Sunday in Advent to post-Pentecost, with 8-line decorated initial: capitulum for vespers (f.13), and 4-line initials for collects: first Sunday in Advent (f.13), Christmas (f.23v), Octave of Christmas (f.31), Epiphany (f.33), Easter (f.66), Ascension (f.74v), Pentecost (f.77), and Trinity Sunday (f.80); ff.95-96 - blank; ff.97-151 - Sanctoral (full Breviary) from SS. Saturninus to Katherine, with 4-line intitials for collects: St Andrew (f.97v), Purification (f.105), St Benedict (f.110v), Annunciation (f.112v), SS. Philip and James (f118v), St John the Baptist (f.120), SS. Peter and Paul (f.125), St Lawrence (f.134), Assumption (f.136v), Birth of the Virgin (f.140), and All Saints (f.146v); ff.152-197v - the Communal (including the Office of the Virgin); ff.197v-212 - the Office of the Dead, and Commendation of Souls; ff.212-214 - Graces for Meals; ff.214-216 - Blessing of Water; f.216v - additions in later hand, including prayers for Visitation Octave and prayer for the scribe. Paper fly-leaves have marginalia, prayers and music. Binding: Late 16th or early 17th

26664.t: Ceremonial, for the use of a cardinal
26664.c: Ceremonial for the use of a bishop or cardinal, as explained in the opening. Contents: Opening (f.1), which begins 'Incipit liber cerimonialis de ministerio Episcopi vel presbiteri Cardinalis servientis pape Missarum solempnia celebrati in officio Capellani, Rubrica, Sciendum et quod Romano pontifico missarum solempnia celebranti servire solet...'. Includes liturgical directions ascribed to the authority of the antipope Benedict XIII in 1410 (f.38) and 1408 (f.42) and to popes Gregory XI (1370-1378, f.47), Clement VI (1342-1352, f.69v) and Alexander IV (1254-1261, ff.143v-144v). Some marginalia. Collation: i-iii10, iv-xii14, xiii-xiv16, xv14 [of 16, 4 blank, last pasted down, lacking 2 further blanks at end]. Horizontal catchwords. Layout: Single column, 27 lines, vertical lines ruled in blind on the vellum leaves and in plummet on the paper leaves, horizontal lines ruled in pale ink. Written space 14 x 8 cm. Script: Written in a rather disjointed round humanistic hand. Decoration: On f.1, a large 8-line initial in blue introduces the text. On f.74 a 6-line initial painted in Romanesque style has a blue surround with brown trefoil corner lobes, infilled with blue arabesques terminating in white (vellum) flowers on a green and brown ground. Colours are in ink washes. Headings are in pale red. Capitals touched in yellow. Paragraph marks in red. 3-line initials throughout in blue or red. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989).

a: Great Britain. Parliament. House of Commons
26873.c: Manuscript relating the proceedings in the House of Commons to impeach the Lord of Clarendon. Binding: Vellum binding with title on front cover: 'Impeachment of Lord Clarendon'. Layout: Written in a single column, 21 lines written space 24.5 x 14.5 cm. Script: Cursive. Catalogued from item in hand and existing card catalogue description. Other title(s): Impeachment of Lord Clarendon. A collection of proceedings in the House of Commons about impeaching the late Earl of Clarendon, then Lord High Chancellor of England, together with the impeachment exhibited against him by the said Commons, with many debates and speeches in the House concerning that matter, as also severall weighty arguments touching the nature of treason by Sir Thomas Osborne, Sir Robt Atkins, Sir Robert Howard, Sir Tho. Littleton & Sergeant Maynard, the then Sollr Generall etc in ye year 1667

27482.c: The second part (Secuna Secundae) of the 'Summa Theologica' of Thomas Aquinas. Binding: 19th century (possibly English) blind-stamped calf, gilt edges (over red). Collation: i6 (table of contents), ii-xxix10, xxx12 [last 2 blank]; with catchwords and some contemporary leaf signatures; medieval foliation excludes the table of contents and reaches [292] at end. Text complete. Layout: Double column, 57 lines, faintly ruled in plummet. Written space 27 x 17.6 cm. Script: Regular gothic bookhand. Decoration: Large 8-line initial on f.1 in divided blue with fine red penwork infilling and surround extending up and down the full height of the page. 2-line initials throughout in red or blue. Headings in red. Many headings for the rubricator visible in lower margins. Capitals touched in red. Paragraph-marks throughout in red or blue. Running-titles in red. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Other title(s): Summa theologica. Secunda secundae. Summa theologica. Pars secunda [title previously supplied by cataloguer]

28021.c: An early manuscript of the 'Summa de casibus' of the Franciscan Astesanus de Ast, dedicated to Giovanni Cajeton circa 1317. Binding: 18th century Flemish orange-brown calf with a coat of arms scratched off each board. Red spine label: 'Astexani summa de casibus Libri 8'. Collation: Lacks first leaf, a leaf after f.109, 2 leaves after f.204 and 2 leaves at end, otherwise complete. Catchwords in decorative cartouches and contemporary ad hoc leaf signatures on outer corners of rectos. Layout: Written in double column, 68 lines, ruled in plummet. Written space 30.8 x 19.6 cm. Script: Small and regular rounded bookhand. Decoration: Six initials (2 of 5-line, 1 each of 4-, 8-, 9- and 10- line) in pink or blue with contrasting surrounds heightened with white tracery and with ivy-leaf infills in red, blue and orange on burnished gold grounds introduce Books I, II, III, V, VI, VIII. They have ivy leaf sprays with (in two instances) dragons. 3-line initials throughout in red or blue with pen-work in black or red; some line-fillers in red or blue with black penwork. Many medieval side-notes, a few tiny sketches of fingers, faces etc. Catalogued from item in hand, catalogue cards and existing description in Manion, Vines and de Hamel (1989). Title supplied by cataloguer. Other Title(s): Summa de casibus

28024.c: A single leaf from a Bible written in Paris between 1280-1290. The text is in Latin, from Saint Jerome’s translation of the Hebrew, and is from the first book of Kings, chapter 4 verse 19 to chapter 8 verse 22. It tells of the Ark of the Covenant in Philistine through to Israel’s demand for a King. With: An enlarged marked-up photocopy of the text, transcript and translation; and a paper by Keith Stuart prepared for the ANZBS Conference, 6-7 December 2010, titled: '1 Kings 4:19-8:22. Text as artefact - an archivist's perspective'. Layout: Double column, 53 lines, ruled in plummet. Script: Written in a small gothic text hand. Decoration: Running titles alternately in red and blue letters. 2-line chapter initials in red and blue with contrasting penwork. Versal initials marked in red. Catalogued from item in hand and existing description from the original vendor. Title supplied by cataloguer.

39752.t: Methods of tracing the genealogy of [some] Islamic mystical paths
39752.c: This manuscript is a treatise showing the genealogy of some mystical paths (tariqats). It includes: al-silsilah al-muhammadiyyah fi tariqah al-'alwaniyyah ['Alwani path], that ends with Hasan al-Basri, 'Ali bin Abi Talib and then Muhammad; al-silsilah al-muhamadiyyah wa al-tariqah al-Qadariyyah [Qadiri path by 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani; as taught by the Qutub (pole) Ahmad al-Kabir al-Qadiri al-Baghdadi], and ends with Hasan al-Basri, 'Ali bin Abi Talib and then Muhammad; and finally al-silsilah Muhammadiyyah wa al-tariqah al-rifa'iyyah (Rifa'i Path; [founded] by the godly pole, Muhammad bin Sayyid Ahmad al-Kabir al-Rifa'i) and ends with Hasan al-Basri, 'Ali bin Abi Talib and Muhammad. The manuscript ends with an incomplete supplicatory appendix. It has paper covers, and is not sewn.

39789.c: The manuscript contains the Arabic ahadith (Islamic traditions) by Muhammad, with the importance of seeking knowledge; the features of Muslim believers (men and women); the inhabitants of Paradise; the best day of death (which will be, according to this manuscript, al-jumu'ah or Layla al-jumu'ah/Friday or Friday night); visiting tombs (ziyarat al-qubur) and also mention of the four rightly Caliphs: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, and 'Ali. On page 1, the name of Muhammad Qasim bin Himzanwayia Milka [?] is written at right angles to the main body of text. The wrapper title reads: Religious instructions by Mohamed. There are red seals on page 1, ink bleed through on multiple pages and the pages are sewn together along the spine.

39813.t: Manuscript wordlist in Persian, Urdu and Arabic
39813.c: The manuscript begins with, 'In the name of God The compassionate the Merciful' and then lists various names with their synonyms in different languages with interlinear Urdu translations. Persian is the main language used throughout the manuscript. It lists weather, phases of the moon and the names of plants and trees, etc. This may possibly be a supplemental text to accompany GMS 100. Wrapper title reads: Arabic & Turkish vocabulary. The manuscript text is written in lines of alternating red and black ink with two languages per line. The manuscript is unbound, has damage to the edges, especially along the head and tail, and also some insect damage. Very fragile.

39826.c: An Arabic manuscript with an emphasis on religious, spiritual, scientific and theological elements. There are references to important figures such as Hasan al-BaSri, Socrates, Raghib, etc., along with short stories and points dealing with important figures such as Alexander the Great. It appears to have been written by an experience writer. Most pages have footnotes or additions, which are written at an angle to the main text. These are mostly in the margins, but some are within the body of the text. Paginated at the time of creation, it consists only of pages 98 to 100. A note on the wrapper corroborates this, referring to the manuscript as a 'fragment'. The wrapper title reads: Gleanings. The manuscript is unbound and has damage to the edges, especially along the tail. Fragile.

39850.c: The author, Sayyid Muhammad Nasir al-Din also known as Muhammad Fatih al-Din ibn Sayyid Muhammad Shad(?) al-Din al-Maghribi, produced this Persian version, with references to Muhammad, for his dear friends ('azizan) who wished to read a simple treatise on rah-i suluk (the path of mystical journey). The author also suggests referring to two other treatises: Risala Qamariyya and Shamsiyya. It was completed Friday noon, 18 Rabi' al-Akhir 1072 AH (circa 1661 AD) in an unidentified location.

45137.t: Comentarius: that is the book of remembrance or register of the history, actions and nature, etc., of me, Emanuel Demetrius, and mine, 1570-1649
45137.c: A handwritten personal diary entitled 'Comentarius: dat is ghedachetenis boeck of te register vande gheschiedenissen handel ende wesen etc. van mij Emmanuel Demetrius en de mijne. 1570' [Comentarius: that is the book of remembrance or register of the history, actions and nature, etc., of me, Emmanuel Demetrius, and mine, 1570], composed by Emmanuel Demetrius van Meteren the Elder, a Flemish merchant and historian living in London, covering his life to 1535 to 1588, featuring key life and political events, including family records, genealogies, quotations, poems, and small colour miniatures. The diary is dedicated to his thirteen children and later entries have been added by his sons Jacob and Emmanuel the Younger, with the last entry dated 16 March 1649. It also includes two coloured portraits of Emmanuel the Elder and his second wife, Hester van Corput, painted on vellum on facing pages, dated 1576 and attributed to Flemish painter, book illuminator, emblematist, and poet Joris Hoefnagel.
